html:
SMTO-EXE-0175 — SMTO's document change request wasn't valid

GUID: 13d45d0c-f244-5f24-a7a8-f785cb2cc24c
Slug: office-invalid-request
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO asked for a document change in a way the document tool doesn't accept, such as a wrong sheet name or missing details. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to read the document first, for example to list the sheets, slides or headings, then repeat your change. SMTO needs the exact names and positions from the current document to describe the change correctly.
  2. Use exact names in your request, and keep sheet names to 31 characters without \ / * ? : [ or ]. Spreadsheet apps don't allow those characters in sheet names.
  3. Ask for one change at a time if the request combined several. Smaller requests are easier to check and less likely to mix up settings.
  4. If every document change fails on one Gateway, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. An older Gateway may not recognize newer document actions.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the edited document without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the change you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO. Your original document isn't changed by a refused request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Office request validation rejected the operation or arguments (office.invalid_request): unknown operation, schema or envelope violation, invalid sheet or object name, an update with no fields, incompatible chart/table/image parameters, or a request the selected Gateway's contract does not accept.

What this means

  • Closed-schema or document-specific argument validation rejected an unsupported operation, invalid name, incompatible chart/table/image parameters or another malformed typed request. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Closed-schema or document-specific argument validation rejected an unsupported operation, invalid name, incompatible chart/table/image parameters or another malformed typed request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact requested operation and format-specific fields with its schema and current object references.

How to fix it

  • Rebuild the request from the advertised Office schema with bounded values and the current expected_revision and object refs from a fresh read (sheet names: 1-31 characters, no \ / * ? : [ ], no leading or trailing quote). If valid requests are rejected only by one Gateway, update that Gateway so its OfficeRequest contract matches the runtime.
  • Use the advertised schema, bounded values and exact revision/object references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the advertised schema, bounded values and exact revision/object references.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid bounded request targets the intended current document structure before editing.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
